hypothesis: One-token lazy parsing will improve size by skipping a match when the next-position match is at least two bytes longer.
change_summary: Add optional cl mode with one-byte lookahead; preserve greedy mode and v1 decoder format.
notes: -0.937% size overall; Canterbury -2.261%; encode speed -18.992%; no per-file size regressions; no external Pareto point. Full results: results/exp-0001/.

hypothesis: Independent 64 KiB blocks with raw fallback will eliminate incompressible expansion and reduce match-state memory without unacceptable aggregate regressions.
change_summary: Add v2 cb/clb modes with nine-byte raw-or-LZ block headers and strict version-aware decoding.
notes: Versus v1 lazy: size -4.503%; encode +24.273%; decode +3.549%; encoder RSS -44.828%. Canterbury size +7.106%; raw/scientific/RGB about -11%. Retain v1 for cross-block compression. Full results: results/exp-0002/.

hypothesis: Block-static entropy coding of LZ token payloads will close a meaningful part of the Canterbury and structured-text gap after exact table costs.
change_summary: Add cbh/clbh modes that select the smallest of raw, plain LZ, or serialized-tree Huffman-coded LZ per v2 block.
notes: Versus blocked lazy: size -9.606%; encode -12.902%; decode -20.754%; RSS +4.425%. Canterbury -22.057%; no per-file size regressions; 1.509% larger than gzip-1 and slower. Full results: results/exp-0003/.

hypothesis: Two-byte matches for distance <=1024 and length <=35 will outweigh four-byte escapes and improve the blocked size/speed frontier.
change_summary: Test an exact-selected variable-match payload beside fixed LZ; revert implementation after rejection.
notes: Versus blocked lazy: size -1.161%; encode -37.960%; decode -7.119%; RSS +5.900%. Nearly all size gain came from generated pseudo-executable; only four small Canterbury files improved. Full results: results/exp-0004/.

hypothesis: Seeding each 64 KiB block with up to 65,535 prior bytes will recover cross-boundary matches while preserving raw fallback and bounded state.
change_summary: Add cblink/clblink v2 mode 4 with one prior-window match history and no second parse.
notes: Versus independent lazy: size -2.286%; encode -20.386%; decode +0.556% noise; RSS +4.734%. Recovers nearly all v1 structured-category ratio with bounded state. Screen and validation: results/exp-0005-screen/ and results/exp-0005/.

hypothesis: Exact-selected Huffman coding over linked-history token payloads will compound the two strongest size mechanisms and approach gzip-1 size.
change_summary: Add cblinkh/clblinkh v2 mode 5 selecting raw, linked LZ, or serialized-tree Huffman-linked LZ.
notes: Versus independent Huffman lazy: size -2.002%; encode -22.589%; decode -5.227%; RSS +18.927%. Size is 0.523% below gzip-1, but zstd-1 remains smaller and faster. Screen and validation: results/exp-0006-screen/ and results/exp-0006/.

hypothesis: Separating controls, literals, offset bytes, and lengths into field-specific order-0 alphabets will outperform one mixed token-byte Huffman alphabet after all tree costs.
change_summary: Add cblinks/clblinks v2 mode 6 with five exact-counted Huffman streams over the unchanged linked token sequence.
notes: Versus linked joint Huffman: size -7.773%; encode -19.257%; decode -7.651%; RSS +5.435%; no per-file size regressions. 0.383% smaller than zstd-1 but zstd-3 is smaller and faster. Results: results/exp-0007-screen/ and results/exp-0007/.

hypothesis: Limiting lazy lookahead to current matches under 32 bytes will recover encode speed with negligible aggregate ratio loss.
change_summary: Add clblinksg mode using the retained mode-6 format with a fixed 32-byte lazy-search gate.
notes: Versus full max lazy: size +0.087%; encode +8.188%; RSS -2.344%. Decode timing was inconsistent across screen/validation. Generated source +9.318%; generated text -12.066%; Canterbury +0.074%. Results: results/exp-0008-screen/ and results/exp-0008/.

hypothesis: A data-driven reversible byte-delta at an adaptively selected stride 1-8 will expose compressible structure in raw RGB and scientific blocks.
change_summary: Add clblinksd mode 7: histogram-concentration stride prefilter, reversible delta, independent LZ, and split entropy with exact total-size selection.
notes: Versus mode 6: size -34.804%; encode -20.374%; decode +2.733% noise; RSS -12.401%. RGB -99.655%, scientific -10.593%; no Canterbury change. Creates a dev-corpus encode frontier but is synthetic-data-heavy. Results: results/exp-0009-screen/ and results/exp-0009/.

hypothesis: An 8-bit Huffman prefix table for sufficiently large streams will improve decode throughput without changing the compressed representation.
change_summary: Build a 256-entry lookup for Huffman streams with >=256 symbols; retain tree fallback and dslow control.
notes: Versus identical-stream tree decoder over five repeats: decode +10.837%; size/encode/binary/RSS unchanged. Scientific +50.69%, JSON +23.44%, XML +22.47%, Canterbury +9.42%; some low-benefit categories regress slightly. Results: results/exp-0010-screen/ and results/exp-0010/.

hypothesis: Four previous-byte-class literal alphabets will exploit local structure that one order-0 literal model misses.
change_summary: Test an exact-selected mode with four literal Huffman streams keyed by the previous decoded byte's top two bits; revert after rejection.
notes: Versus delta parent over five repeats: size -0.258%; encode throughput -11.319%; decode throughput -4.535%; encoder RSS +19.940%. Mode 8 won 29/152 blocks across seven files, but 83.6% of the 6,084-byte gain came from generated pseudo_text.bin. Results: results/exp-0011-screen/ and results/exp-0011/.

hypothesis: Persistent circular match chains will remove repeated linked-history indexing while preserving token choices and compressed size.
change_summary: Test clblinksp with a 64-bit head table and circular predecessor-distance array; verify byte-identical output and revert after rejection.
notes: Compressed streams were byte-identical to clblinksd. Over five repeats encode throughput fell 7.132%; decoder throughput differed -2.772% despite identical streams and is noise. The 64-bit hot head table and ring indirection outweighed saved history indexing; generated source alone improved 2.15%. Results: results/exp-0012-screen/ and results/exp-0012/.

hypothesis: A small spatial sample plus a conservative concentration gate will retain useful delta strides while avoiding full histogram scans and discarded transformed parses.
change_summary: Add clblinksdf using at most 4,095 sampled bytes from block start/middle/end and require a 1.2x concentration gain before transformed parsing.
notes: Compressed streams were byte-identical to clblinksd on all 26 dev files. Over five repeats encode throughput improved 15.261% with unchanged size/format; decode -1.316% is identical-stream noise and the RSS maximum was not credited. Selector work fell from 52 transformed parses to 36 while retaining all 34 winning blocks. Results: results/exp-0013-screen/ and results/exp-0013/.

hypothesis: A lazy decision based on estimated raw token-bit density will outperform the current covered-length rule across data distributions.
change_summary: Test a 25-bit match versus 33-bit literal-plus-match local density rule with an upper-bound lookahead gate; revert codec after dual-corpus rejection.
notes: Frozen dev screen: 44 bytes smaller (-0.0019%), encode -0.420%, with 8 files better and 8 worse. Public research screen: 1,407 bytes larger (+0.0326%), encode -6.723%, 4/16 files better and 12/16 worse. Rejected without validation; raw token density did not generalize. Results: results/exp-0014-screen/ and results/exp-0014-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Modulo deltas between consecutive match distances will make the split distance streams more compressible.
change_summary: Test an exact-selected mode 8 that delta-codes the 16-bit distance sequence before the existing low/high Huffman streams; revert after dual-corpus null result.
notes: Mode 8 won zero blocks across 26 dev and 16 public research files, leaving every compressed size unchanged. Generating the extra five-stream representation reduced encode throughput 8.870% on dev and 6.547% on research. Results: results/exp-0015-screen/ and results/exp-0015-research-screen/.

hypothesis: A work-estimated Huffman lookup gate will avoid table construction on streams whose tree-walk savings cannot repay it.
change_summary: Test dwork on identical clblinksdf streams; enable the 256-entry lookup only when encoded-bit work exceeds one edge per symbol plus 2,048 construction edges.
notes: Five-repeat identical-stream decode improved 1.736% on dev and 0.712% on public research, below the established ~3% process-level noise threshold; 5/26 dev and 3/16 research files still regressed. Reverted rather than tune the threshold. Results: results/exp-0016-screen/, exp-0016/, exp-0016-research-screen/, and exp-0016-research/.

hypothesis: The unchanged work-estimated Huffman lookup gate will show a reproducible steady-state decode gain once process startup is removed.
change_summary: Re-test EXP-0016 unchanged with the in-process runner; retain dwork after two reversed-order 30-repeat runs on both routine suites.
notes: Identical size/format. Dev decode +3.038% then +3.746%; public research +1.217% then +0.622%, with sign preserved after reversing codec order. Prior process controls showed unchanged encode/binary/RSS. 60 sanitizer-backed d/dwork streams passed. Results: results/exp-0017-inprocess-dev*/ and results/exp-0017-inprocess-research*/.

hypothesis: A bounded dynamic parser using the parent block's actual split-Huffman field costs will improve ratio broadly enough to justify a maximum-compression mode.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt: precompute longest matches at every position, derive literal/distance/length code costs from the parent parse, optimize literals versus the eight longest match lengths, and exact-select the resulting ordinary mode-6 stream.
notes: Versus clblinksdf over three repeats: dev size -2.509%, encode -70.307%, decode -3.422%, encoder RSS +10.843%; 17/26 files improve and none regress. Public research size -3.616%, all 16 files improve, encode -74.007%, decode -2.968%, RSS +31.471%. Production binary grows 23.816% versus pre-feature. Results: results/exp-0018-screen/, exp-0018/, exp-0018-research-screen/, and exp-0018-research/.

hypothesis: Skipping bounded dynamic parsing when the parent split-Huffman representation does not beat raw storage will recover encode speed without changing selected output.
change_summary: Test clblinksoptg with a parent-split-versus-raw work gate; verify exact streams on all observed files, then revert after the speed gain fails to generalize.
notes: Five-repeat dev output is byte-identical and encode throughput improves 4.239%, but three generated fixtures (random, pseudo_text, RGB) account for 64.6 ms saved versus 59.1 ms aggregate; the remaining dev files regress in aggregate. Public research output is also byte-identical but encode throughput regresses 0.578%. Screen research timing falsely suggested +6.6%; validation reversed it. Results: results/exp-0019-screen/, exp-0019/, exp-0019-research-screen/, and exp-0019-research/.

hypothesis: Re-estimating split-Huffman costs from EXP-0018's optimized parse and parsing once more will capture model/parse convergence gains across data distributions.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2: run exactly one additional cost-model and whole-block DP pass, Huffman-code it as ordinary mode 6, and exact-select it against the first optimized parse.
notes: Versus clblinksopt over three repeats: dev size -0.482% with 15/26 files improved and none worse, encode throughput -39.758%, encoder RSS +7.200%; public research size -0.498% with 14/16 improved and none worse, encode -42.289%, RSS +11.258%. Decode format is unchanged and timing deltas are not credited. Candidate remains dominated by cached xz-6 on dev, so this is an internal maximum-ratio point, not an external frontier claim. Results: results/exp-0020-screen/, exp-0020/, exp-0020-research-screen/, and exp-0020-research/.

hypothesis: For each candidate match length, selecting the lowest modeled-cost distance from the bounded hash chain will beat using only the longest match's distance.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2d: after EXP-0020's two passes, run one exact-selected DP whose eight candidate lengths each use the lowest split-Huffman distance cost among up to 64 chain matches.
notes: Versus clblinksopt2 over three process repeats: dev size -0.737% with 15/26 files improved and none worse, encode throughput -68.119%, encoder RSS +62.439%; public research size -0.767% with all 16 files improved, encode -47.595%, RSS +11.330%. A three-repeat in-process dev control measures decode -0.377% (280.09 versus 281.15 MB/s), rejecting the noisy process-level -10.4% result. Binary size and decoder representation are unchanged. Cached xz-6 still dominates this internal endpoint. Results: results/exp-0021-screen/, exp-0021/, exp-0021-research-screen/, exp-0021-research/, and exp-0021-inprocess-dev/.

hypothesis: Enumerating costed-distance matches inside the backward DP and storing only the selected offset will preserve EXP-0021's stream while reducing encoder memory without slowing it.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2df: build predecessor chains once, enumerate the same bounded candidates during backward optimization, and replace eight offsets per position with one selected offset.
notes: Streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2d on all 43 observed files. Over three repeats, dev encoder RSS falls 11.931% and public research RSS falls 10.253%; encode throughput changes -0.091% and +0.297%, both noise. Decode, compressed size, format, and binary behavior are unchanged; the compiled binary grows only 32 bytes versus EXP-0021. Results: results/exp-0022-screen/, exp-0022/, exp-0022-research-screen/, and exp-0022-research/.

hypothesis: Sharing one immutable predecessor-chain and longest-match index across all optimized parses will preserve EXP-0022's stream while recovering substantial encode speed.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2dfs: build the per-block match index once, reuse longest matches for both normal DP passes, and reuse predecessor chains for fused costed-distance enumeration.
notes: Streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2df on all 43 observed files. Over three repeats, dev encode throughput improves 15.709% with RSS +0.746%; public research improves 25.347% with RSS +3.777%. Size, format, and decode behavior are exact controls; process decode differences are noise. The compiled binary is 92,552 bytes (+96 versus EXP-0022). Results: results/exp-0023-screen/, exp-0023/, exp-0023-research-screen/, and exp-0023-research/.

hypothesis: Exact-selecting joint-Huffman and split-Huffman models for each optimized parse will recover blocks where five split trees cost more than field separation saves.
change_summary: Test joint mode-5 encoding of all three already-generated optimized token streams against their mode-6 encodings, then revert after a dual-corpus zero-win result.
notes: Candidate streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2dfs on all 43 observed files, proving optimized joint Huffman wins zero blocks. One-repeat encode screens change -1.776% dev and -1.688% public research; timing was not validated because deterministic size supplied no positive signal. Parent mode 5 already covers joint-coding wins from the original parse. Results: results/exp-0024-screen/ and exp-0024-research-screen/.

hypothesis: When the first optimized parse is byte-identical to its parent, skipping the provably redundant second normal DP will preserve output and recover meaningful encode speed.
change_summary: Test an exact token-stream fixed-point check; on equality, reuse the first parse as the cost model for the costed-distance pass and skip the second normal parse plus split encode.
notes: Streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2dfs on all 43 observed files, confirming correctness of the fixed-point rule. One-repeat encode screens improve only 0.439% on dev and 0.011% on public research, both far below the 3% process-noise threshold; no validation was warranted. The exact condition is too rare or covers too little work to create a practical point. Results: results/exp-0025-screen/ and exp-0025-research-screen/.
